issue: Does a prisoner who wins resentencing relief in a habeas case get to challenge his undisturbed underlying conviction in a second-in-time petition without that petition being barred as second or successive under 28 U.S.C. § 2244(b)?

sides.position: A prisoner who obtains relief as to his sentence is not barred from raising, in a second-in-time habeas petition, a challenge to an undisturbed conviction (the majority interpretation, following Magwood).
cases: Johnson v. United States, 623 F.3d 41 (2d Cir. 2010)
Lesko v. Secretary Pennsylvania Department of Corrections, 34 F.4th 211 (3d Cir. 2022)
United States v. Hill, 98 F.4th 473 (3d Cir. 2024)

sides.position: The contrary view described as the minority position, under which a challenge to an undisturbed conviction in a later petition is treated as second or successive under § 2244(b). The excerpt says a split exists but does not name the circuits on this side.

this_court: Follows the majority interpretation: a prisoner who receives relief as to his sentence may raise a challenge to an undisturbed conviction in a second-in-time petition.
quote: The Lesko panel acknowledged that a circuit split exists after Magwood but sided with the majority of circuits that have considered the issue:
cite: United States v. Carlos Hill, 98 F.4th 473 (3rd Cir. 2024)
